message_list.content: Hi and welcome to Celestar Air. I'm Nova, your virtual flight assistant. Thanks for calling! How can I help you today?
message_list.guideline_text: Start the conversation with a warm greeting and introduction. Use: 'Hi and welcome to Celestar Air. I'm Nova, your virtual flight assistant. Thanks for calling! How can I help you today?'

message_list.content: Hi, I need some help changing my flight booking. I have a ticket for a flight from Seattle to Dallas on April 8th, but I would like to modify it. Could you assist me with that?

Absolutely, I can help with that. Please provide:
- Your new travel date
- Your preferred time window
- Your desired cabin class
message_list.guideline_text: Collect New Schedule Needs: Ask for the new travel date, preferred time window, and desired cabin class for the selected segments.

message_list.content: I would like to change the travel date to April 10th and prefer to keep the same cabin class, which is first. Can you also check if I can upgrade to a more comfortable seat by chance?
To pull up your reservation, please provide your e-ticket number and your last name exactly as it appears on the booking.
message_list.guideline_text: Access Booking By Ticket: Ask for the e-ticket number and last name to pull up the reservation.

message_list.content: My ticket number is 9321992246183 and my last name is Patel.
To verify your identity, please confirm your date of birth.
message_list.guideline_text: Confirm Account Identity: Ask the caller to confirm date of birth to verify identity.

message_list.content: My date of birth is May 12, 1985.
Please confirm which passengers on the reservation you want to update and which flight segments you want to change.
message_list.guideline_text: Define Change Scope: Ask which passengers and which flight segments in the reservation will be updated.

message_list.content: There's just me on this reservation, and it's the outbound flight from Seattle to Dallas that I'd like to change.

Here are two options for your new flight:
- Option 1: Depart 9:30 am, arrive 3:20 pm, duration 3 hours 50 minutes, total change cost 165 dollars
- Option 2: Depart 5:45 pm, arrive 11:30 pm, duration 3 hours 45 minutes, total change cost 95 dollars

Please let me know which option you would like to choose.
message_list.guideline_text: Offer Curated Alternatives: Present two suitable replacement options with flight times, duration, and total change cost and ask the caller to choose one.

message_list.content: I think I'll go with Option 1. Could you also let me know if you can accommodate my service animal on this new flight?
I will transfer you to a human agent who can confirm accommodation for your service animal on your flight. Please hold while I connect you.
message_list.guideline_text: If the caller requests exceptions, disputes eligibility, or needs determinations about service animal documentation/acceptance, transfer to a human agent. If they only ask general requirements, provide policy information.

message_list.content: Thank you. While I'm waiting, could I also receive some information on the refund policy in case my plans change again?

Please complete payment using this secure link: https://pay.celestarair.com/secure/8H3K2N9Q
For your security, do not share your card details here.
After payment, reply with the one-time transaction ID and your billing country only.
message_list.guideline_text: Take Payment Details: Provide a secure payment link and explicitly tell the user not to share card details, then ask them to reply with the one-time transaction ID and their billing country only.

message_list.content: Could you tell me about the refund policy first? I'd like to know my options just in case.

Here is a quick overview of our refund policy for First Class tickets. Eligibility depends on whether your fare is refundable or nonrefundable.

- 24 hour flexible cancellation: Full refund if you cancel within 24 hours of original purchase and the booking was made at least 7 days before departure.
- Refundable First Class fares: Fully refundable to the original form of payment any time before departure. If partially flown, the unused portion is refunded.
- Nonrefundable First Class fares for domestic travel: No change fees. If you cancel before departure, the ticket value becomes a travel credit valid for 12 months from the original issue date. Cash refunds are not available except in the disruption cases below.
- No show: If you do not cancel before the scheduled departure, the remaining ticket value is forfeited.
- Airline schedule change or cancellation: If we cancel your flight or cause a schedule change of 2 hours or more, you can request a full refund to your original form of payment.
- Paid seats or comfort upgrades: If we cannot honor the seat or upgrade you purchased, that fee is refunded. Otherwise these fees are nonrefundable once flown or if you voluntarily cancel.
- Refund timing: Refunds to credit cards are processed within 7 business days after approval. Refunds to other payment methods are processed within 20 business days.
message_list.guideline_text: If the caller requests exceptions, disputes eligibility, or needs determinations about service animal documentation/acceptance, transfer to a human agent. If they only ask general requirements, provide policy information.

message_list.content: Great, thank you for that information. One last thing, I've also got some high-value items in my luggage that I've recently realized might need special attention if anything were to happen. Could you assist me in understanding my options for those?

Absolutely. Here are practical options to help protect high-value items when you travel:

- Keep them with you in carry-on whenever possible. Avoid checking jewelry, electronics, important documents, cash, and similar valuables.
- If you must check them, ask at the airport to declare a higher value for your checked bag for an added fee where offered. Liability limits and exclusions apply, so verify what is covered before purchase.
- Consider travel insurance that specifically covers high-value personal items. Confirm per-item limits, total coverage, and any exclusions.
- Use discreet, hard-sided luggage with a sturdy lock, and avoid external tags that indicate valuable contents.
- Add a tracking tag inside the bag and enable device and airline notifications.
- Pack valuables in padded cases, photograph contents, note serial numbers, and keep purchase receipts.
- Place your name and contact details inside and outside the bag.
- At check-in, request a fragile handling tag and let the agent know the bag needs careful handling. Retrieve the bag promptly on arrival.

If you would like, I can summarize these into a quick pre-trip checklist.
message_list.guideline_text: If the caller reports lost/delayed baggage containing high-value items, medicine, passports, or irreplaceable items and requests exception/compensation determination, transfer to a human agent.

message_list.content: Could you help me with compensation options if my luggage with these high-value items gets lost or delayed?

I can share how compensation typically works if a checked bag with high-value items is lost or delayed.

- Lost checked bag
  - Standard airline liability applies with a capped amount per passenger, and many high-value items like jewelry, electronics, cash, and important documents are limited or excluded.
  - If you purchased declared excess valuation at check-in and it is accepted for your items, that higher limit applies for a loss.
  - Travel insurance or eligible credit card baggage coverage can reimburse high-value items beyond airline limits, subject to policy terms and documentation.

- Delayed checked bag
  - You can be reimbursed for reasonable essential purchases while the bag is delayed, with receipts required and per-day or total caps. High-value contents are not typically covered for delay itself. If the bag is later deemed lost, the claim is then handled under lost bag rules.

- If this happens
  - Report it immediately at the baggage service desk and obtain a file reference number.
  - Keep all receipts and submit your claim within the stated deadline on your claim form.

message_list.content: Alright, but let's say the lost or delayed luggage contains important documents or irreplaceable items like my passport. What happens in that case for compensations?
I will transfer you to a human agent who can review exceptions and compensation for high-value or irreplaceable items such as a passport. Please hold while I connect you.
